text: THE STAGE-PX-TO-FRAME-PX CONVERSION THE CORPUS USES IS RIGHT ON ONE AXIS ONLY. Two upheld findings convert the recovered reach into screen pixels at 'x2.4 screen px per stage px in a 1080p capture' (LEDGER_EVIDENCE.md:3084 and :3370), from the stage width. I opened the constants on the WEB side, not just the android side: §1t1523s0§.as:104 'public static var stageWidth:int = 800;' and :106 'public static var stageHeight:int = 480;' (android StatsManager.as:80, :82 identical). 800 x 480 is 5:3. A 1920 x 1080 capture is 16:9. 1920/800 = 2.40 but 1080/480 = 2.25, so no single uniform scale maps the game stage onto a 1080p frame - the capture is either width-fit and vertically cropped or overflowed, or height-fit at 2.25 and pillarboxed. InputManager.as:223-224 confirms a runtime scale exists and is applied as '(args.stageX - StatsManager.stageOffsetX) / StatsManager.stageScale', with an offset on both axes, i.e. the game explicitly supports letterboxing. WHY IT MATTERS HERE: RR:190 blocker (1) asked for the reach 'in stage px' precisely so it could be checked against footage. The formula is recovered, but the last step - stage px to frame px - is being done with a factor that cannot be right for both axes, and a blade path is drawn diagonally, so it uses both. WHAT IS NOT CLOSED: which fit the two longplays used. That needs one frame (A1) measuring a known-width stage element, and I did not open one - STILL_UNHELD is the honest answer for that half.
